title: Vincent Massey appointed first Canada-born Governor General of Canada
text: Charles Vincent Massey was a Canadian diplomat and statesman who served as the 18th governor general of Canada from 1952 to 1959. Massey was the first governor general of Canada to be born in Canada.

title: Elizabeth II becomes Queen of Canada upon the death of her father George VI.
text: Elizabeth II was Queen of the United Kingdom and other Commonwealth realms from 6 February 1952 until her death in 2022. She was queen regnant of 32 sovereign states during her lifetime and was the monarch of 15 realms at her death.

title: Saskatchewan election: Tommy Douglas's Co-operative Commonwealth Federation wins a third consecutive majority
text: Thomas Clement Douglas was a Scottish-born Canadian politician who served as the seventh premier of Saskatchewan from 1944 to 1961 and leader of the New Democratic Party from 1961 to 1971. A Baptist minister, he was elected to the House of Commons of Canada in 1935 as a member of the Co-operative Commonwealth Federation (CCF).

title: Korean War: Canadian troops are dispatched to the troubled Geoje POW Camp
text: The Korean War was an armed conflict fought on the Korean Peninsula between North Korea (Democratic People's Republic of Korea; DPRK) and South Korea (Republic of Korea; ROK) and their allies. North Korea was supported by China and the Soviet Union, while South Korea was supported by the United Nations led by the United States under the auspices of the United Nations Command (UNC).

title: Quebec election: Maurice Duplessis' Union Nationale wins a third consecutive majority
text: Maurice Le Noblet Duplessis, popularly known as "Le Chef" (, "The Boss"), was a Canadian lawyer and politician who served as the 16th premier of Quebec. A conservative, nationalist, populist, anti-communist, anti-unionist, and fervent Catholic, Duplessis and his party, the Union Nationale, dominated provincial politics from the 1920s to the 1950s.

title: W.A.C. Bennett becomes premier of British Columbia, replacing Byron Johnson
text: William Andrew Cecil Bennett was a Canadian politician who served as the 25th premier of British Columbia from 1952 to 1972. With just over 20 years in office, Bennett remains the longest-serving premier in British Columbia history.

title: Alberta election: Ernest Manning's Social Credit Party wins a fifth consecutive majority
text: Ernest Charles Manning was a Canadian politician and the eighth premier of Alberta between 1943 and 1968 for the Social Credit Party of Alberta. He served for 25 years, longer than any other premier in the province's history and the second longest-serving provincial premier in Canadian history (after George Henry Murray of Nova Scotia).

title: The first CBC Television station, CBFT, goes on the air in Montreal, Quebec
text: CBFT-DT is a television station in Montreal, Quebec, Canada, serving as the flagship station of the French-language service of Ici Radio-Canada Télé. It is owned and operated by the Canadian Broadcasting Corporation (known in French as Société Radio-Canada) alongside CBC Television outlet CBMT-DT (channel 6).

title: CBLT (CBC Toronto) goes on air
text: CBLT-DT is a television station in Toronto, Ontario, Canada, serving as the flagship station of the English-language service of CBC Television. It is part of a twinstick with Ici Radio-Canada Télé outlet CBLFT-DT (channel 25).

title: The Boyd Gang is captured
text: The Boyd Gang was a notorious criminal gang based in Toronto, Ontario, Canada, named for member Edwin Alonzo Boyd. The gang was famous in the media at the time because of their actions, which included bank robberies, jail breaks, relationships with women, gun fights, manhunts, and captures.

title: Hugh John Flemming becomes premier of New Brunswick, replacing John McNair
text: The premier of New Brunswick or première ministre du Nouveau-Brunswick (feminine)) is the first minister and head of government for the Canadian province of New Brunswick. The premier of a Canadian province is much like the prime minister of Canada.

title: Lester B. Pearson is elected President of the United Nations General Assembly.
text: Lester Bowles Pearson was a Canadian politician, diplomat, and scholar who served as the 14th prime minister of Canada from 1963 to 1968. He also served as leader of the Liberal Party from 1958 to 1968 and as leader of the Official Opposition from 1958 to 1963.

title: The pension system is reformed with the introduction of the Old Age Security Act.
text: The Old Age Security program is a universal retirement pension available to most residents and citizens of Canada who have reached 65 years old. This pension is supplemented by the Guaranteed Income Supplement (GIS), which is added to the monthly OAS payment for seniors with lower incomes.

title: Roy Thomson acquires The Scotsman and emigrates to Britain
text: Roy Herbert Thomson, 1st Baron Thomson of Fleet, was a Canadian-born British newspaper proprietor who became one of the moguls of Fleet Street in London. He first came to prominence when he was selling radios in Ontario, and to give his customers more programmes to listen to, decided to launch his own radio station.
wiki: Roy Thomson, 1st Baron Thomson of Fleet

title: Atomic Energy Canada founded.
text: Atomic Energy of Canada Limited is a Canadian Crown corporation and the largest nuclear science and technology laboratory in Canada. AECL developed the CANDU reactor technology starting in the 1950s, and in October 2011 licensed this technology to Candu Energy.

title: Canada men's national ice hockey team (represented by the Edmonton Mercurys) win their 7th (consecutive and last until 2002) Gold Medal at the 1952 Winter Olympics in Oslo, Norway
text: The Canada men's national ice hockey team is the ice hockey team representing Canada internationally. The team is overseen by Hockey Canada, a member of the International Ice Hockey Federation.
wiki: Canada men's national ice hockey team

title: The Detroit Red Wings win their fifth Stanley Cup by defeating the Montreal Canadiens 4 games to 0.
text: The Stanley Cup is the championship trophy awarded annually to the National Hockey League (NHL) playoff champion. It is the oldest existing trophy to be awarded to a professional sports franchise in North America, and the International Ice Hockey Federation (IIHF) considers it to be one of the "most important championships available to the sport".

title: The Ontario Hockey Association's Guelph Biltmores win their only Memorial Cup by defeating the Saskatchewan Junior Hockey League's Regina Pats 4 games to 0. The deciding Game 4 was played at Maple Leaf Gardens in Toronto
text: The Ontario Hockey League) is one of the three major junior ice hockey leagues which constitute the Canadian Hockey League, alongside the Western Hockey League and the Quebec Maritimes Junior Hockey League. The league is for players aged 16–20.

title: The Toronto Argonauts win their tenth (and last until 1983) Grey Cup by defeating the Edmonton Eskimos 21–11 in the 40th Grey Cup played at Toronto's Varsity Stadium
text: The Grey Cup is both the championship game of the Canadian Football League (CFL) and the trophy awarded to the victorious team playing in the namesake championship of professional Canadian football. The game is contested between the winners of the CFL's East and West divisional playoffs and is one of Canadian television's largest annual sporting events.

title: Thomas B. Costain: The Silver Chalice
text: Thomas Bertram Costain was a Canadian-American journalist who became a best-selling author of historical novels at the age of 57.

title: See 1952 Governor General's Awards for a complete list of winners and finalists for those awards.
text: In Canada, the 1952 Governor General's Awards for Literary Merit were the sixteenth such awards. The awards in this period had no monetary prize and were just an honour for the authors.

title: Stephen Leacock Award: Jan Hilliard, The Salt Box
text: Hilda Kay Grant was a Canadian writer and artist who published both non-fiction work under her own name and novels under the pen name Jan Hilliard.

title: “Blue Tango” by Leroy Anderson
text: "Blue Tango" is an instrumental composition by Leroy Anderson, written for orchestra in 1951 and published in 1952. It was later turned into a popular song with lyrics by Mitchell Parish.
listen: Blue Tango Leroy Anderson

title: “Wheel of Fortune” by Kay Starr
text: "Wheel of Fortune" is a popular song written by Bennie Benjamin and George David Weiss and published in 1951. It is best remembered in the 1952 hit version by Kay Starr.
listen: Wheel of Fortune Kay Starr

title: “Cry” by Johnnie Ray & The Four Lads
text: "Cry" is a 1951 popular song written by Churchill Kohlman. It was first recorded by Ruth Casey on the Cadillac label.
listen: Cry Johnnie Ray & The Four Lads

title: “You Belong to Me” by Jo Stafford with Paul Weston
text: "You Belong to Me" is a popular music ballad from the 1950s. It is well known for its opening line, "See the pyramids along the Nile".
listen: You Belong to Me Jo Stafford with Paul Weston

title: “Auf Wiederseh'n, Sweetheart” by Vera Lynn with Her Majesty's Forces and Roland Shaw
text: "Auf Wiedersehen", or "Auf Wiederseh'n, Sweetheart", is a song written by German composer Eberhard Storch around 1950. Storch wrote the song in the hospital for his wife Maria as he was ill for a long time.
listen: Auf Wiederseh'n, Sweetheart Vera Lynn with Her Majesty's Forces and Roland Shaw

title: “Half as Much” by Rosemary Clooney with Percy Faith
text: "Half as Much" is an American country song written by Curley Williams in 1951. It was recorded by country music singer Hank Williams in 1952 and reached number two on the Billboard Country Singles chart.
listen: Half as Much Rosemary Clooney with Percy Faith

title: “Wish You Were Here” by Eddie Fisher with Hugo Winterhalter
text: "Wish You Were Here" is a popular song with music and lyrics by Harold Rome, the title tune from his 1952 show, Wish You Were Here. It was introduced in the show and on the RCA Victor cast album by Jack Cassidy.
listen: Wish You Were Here Eddie Fisher with Hugo Winterhalter

title: “I Went to Your Wedding” by Patti Page
text: "I Went to Your Wedding" is a popular song written and composed by Jessie Mae Robinson and published in 1952.
listen: I Went to Your Wedding Patti Page

title: “Here in My Heart” by Al Martino
text: "Here in My Heart" is a popular song written by Pat Genaro, Lou Levinson, and Bill Borrelli, first published in 1952. A recording of the song by Italian-American singer Al Martino made history as the first number one hit on the UK singles chart, on November 14, 1952.
listen: Here in My Heart Al Martino

title: “Delicado” by Percy Faith with Stan Freeman
text: "Delicado" is a popular song published in 1952 with music by Waldir Azevedo and lyrics by Jack Lawrence. The song reached the top of the Billboard charts in 1952.
listen: Delicado Percy Faith with Stan Freeman

title: “Kiss of Fire” by Georgia Gibbs with Glenn Osser
text: "El Choclo" is a popular song written by Ángel Villoldo, an Argentine musician. Allegedly written in honour of and taking its title from the nickname of the proprietor of a nightclub, who was known as "El Choclo", it is one of the most popular tangos in Argentina.
listen: Kiss of Fire Georgia Gibbs with Glenn Osser

title: “Anytime” by Eddie Fisher with Hugo Winterhalter
text: "Any Time" is a Tin Pan Alley song written by Herbert "Happy" Lawson. It was published in 1921 and first recorded by Emmett Miller for OKeh Records in 1924, accompanying himself on ukulele, Lawson recorded his own version for Gennett Records on July 31, 1925.
listen: Anytime Eddie Fisher with Hugo Winterhalter

title: “Tell Me Why” by The Four Aces featuring Al Alberts
text: "Tell Me Why" is a popular song written by Marty Gold with the lyrics by Al Alberts. The song was published in 1951.
listen: Tell Me Why The Four Aces featuring Al Alberts

title: “The Blacksmith Blues” by Ella Mae Morse with Nelson Riddle
text: "The Blacksmith Blues" is a song which was written for Ella Mae Morse by Jack Holmes. The recording reached #3 on the Billboard chart when it was released in 1952, and sold over a million copies.
listen: The Blacksmith Blues Ella Mae Morse with Nelson Riddle

title: “Jambalaya (On the Bayou)” by Jo Stafford with Paul Weston and The Norman Luboff Choir
text: "Jambalaya" is a song written and recorded by American country music singer Hank Williams that was first released in July 1952. It is Williams' most recorded song.

title: “Botch-a-Me (Ba-Ba-Baciami Piccina)” by Rosemary Clooney
text: "Botch-a-Me" is a popular song, written in 1940. The original Italian version by Alberto Rabagliati was written by Riccardo Morbelli (words) and Luigi Astore (music).

title: “A Guy Is a Guy” by Doris Day with Paul Weston
text: "A Guy Is a Guy" is a traditional pop song written by Oscar Brand. It was published in 1952.
listen: A Guy Is a Guy Doris Day with Paul Weston

title: “The Little White Cloud That Cried” by Johnnie Ray & The Four Lads
text: "The Little White Cloud that Cried" is a popular song written by Johnnie Ray and published in 1951. The biggest hit version was recorded by Ray and The Four Lads in 1951.

title: “High Noon” by Frankie Laine
text: "The Ballad of High Noon" is a popular song published in 1952, with music by Dimitri Tiomkin and lyrics by Ned Washington. It is the theme song of the 1952 multiple Academy Award-winning movie High Noon (and titled onscreen as such in the film's opening credits as sung by popular country music singer and actor Tex Ritter), with its tune repeated throughout the film.
listen: High Noon Frankie Laine

title: “I'm Yours” by Eddie Fisher with Hugo Winterhalter
text: "I'm Yours" is a 1952 popular song by Robert Mellin. Recordings of it were made by Eddie Fisher, Don Cornell, The Four Aces, and Toni Arden.
listen: I'm Yours Eddie Fisher with Hugo Winterhalter

title: “The Glow-Worm” by The Mills Brothers and Hal McIntyre
text: "Das Glühwürmchen", known in English as "The Glow-Worm", is a song from Paul Lincke's 1902 operetta Lysistrata, with German lyrics by Heinz Bolten-Backers. In the operetta, it is performed as a trio with three female solo voices singing alternately and the women's chorus joining in the refrain.

title: “It's in the Book” by Johnny Standley with Horace Heidt
text: "It's in the Book" is a recorded comic monologue by Johnny Standley. It was marketed as a pop song and made the Billboard chart in 1952, reaching number one.

title: “I'll Walk Alone”
text: "I'll Walk Alone" is a 1944 popular song with music by Jule Styne and lyrics by Sammy Cahn. The song was written for the 1944 musical film Follow the Boys, in which it was sung by Dinah Shore, and was nominated for the Academy Award for Best Original Song but lost to “Swinging on a Star”.

title: “Trying” by The Hilltoppers
text: "Trying" is a song written by Billy Vaughn and performed by The Hilltoppers. It reached number 5 on the Cashbox chart and number 7 on the U.S. Billboard pop chart in 1952.

title: “Please, Mr. Sun” by Johnnie Ray & The Four Lads
